html:
Caracas is the capital of Venezuela, in a mountain valley near the Caribbean coast. The Spanish captain Diego de Losada founded it on 25 July 1567, after years of war with the local peoples.

It grew as the centre of a rich cacao trade and became the seat of the Captaincy General of Venezuela in 1777. Its creole elite, enriched by cacao estates worked by enslaved Africans, produced both Francisco de Miranda and Simón Bolívar, and the city led the declaration of independence in 1811.

The earthquake of 1812 destroyed much of it. In the 1900s oil money turned it into a city of highways and towers, ringed by hillside slums. It was the stage of the Caracazo in 1989 and of the politics of Venezuela ever since.
sum: Caracas is the capital of Venezuela, in a mountain valley near the Caribbean coast. The Spanish captain Diego de Losada founded it on 25 July 1567, after years of war with the local peoples.
